relationship: Wrapping application data in protocol layers connects TCP/IP encapsulation to a packet's journey and receiver unpacking.

learnerLoop.action: Add or peel outer protocol wrappers at the sender, then send the built packet.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The packet gains or loses the selected protocol shells as it moves between hosts.
learnerLoop.evidence: The packing mat, flight packet, receiver packet and status strip show each layer's role.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Add, remove or compare wrappers and explain what the receiver must unpack.

invariants: The packet shells shown in flight and at the receiver match the wrappers selected.
Receiver peeling removes the outer visible shell in order.
safeAdaptations: Change application stories, endpoint labels or prompts while preserving layer construction and ordered unpacking.
nonGoals: Sending a real TCP/IP packet or emulating complete network protocols.

task.description: Deliver the browser request to the web process, then compare delivery to mail.
task.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

model.description: Shell rack, sender packing mat, link and receiver preserve the original spatial sequence. Remaining-layer tokens travel in a dedicated receiver lane.
model.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

controls.description: Add a protocol shell, peel only the outer one, send any constructed order and reset.
controls.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

evidence.description: Layer-specific acceptance/rejection and exact header reads beside the remaining layers, without covering the gates.
evidence.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

stack.domain: Expected inner-to-outer TCP, IP, Link; each wrapper used once.
stack.output: Nested packet and remaining receiver packet.

addressing.domain: Fixed IPv4/MAC addresses; source port 49152, HTTP destination 80 or SMTP 25.

modes.process: Web initially; Compare another process unlocks after Web success and switches to Mail.
modes.support: No Working or exam toggle; all wrappers remain learner actions.

dependencies: The receiver first expects Link, then IP, then TCP.
Any incorrect outer order stops at the corresponding receiver gate.
Web delivery must succeed before Mail comparison.
implementation.completion: The correct original application payload reaches the chosen process after all three headers are consumed; success is recorded per service.
limitations: One application message in one packet on one direct Ethernet link; excludes DNS, routing, handshakes, congestion and retransmission.
